title: Industrial Production and Capacity Utilization (G.17, November 2026 data) — 9:15 a.m. ET, the December twin sharing a GDPNow vintage with two already-tracked releases
source: EST: federalreserve.gov/feeds/g17.html fetched direct 2026-09-06 (HTTP 200, 614,006 bytes), the Board's own scheduling notice, verbatim: "In 2026, the G.17 release on Industrial Production and Capacity Utilization will be published at 9:15 a.m. on ... November 17, and December 16." Corroborated by the Board's release-date table (releases/g17/release_dates.htm, HTTP 200, 117,098 bytes), row "December 2026 | 16-December-2026", and by the Atlanta Fed's GDPNowcastDataReleaseDates.xlsx PostedUpdates sheet, whose 2026-12-16 row reads "Retail sales + inventories, Industrial production". Filed estimate per the lane's no-self-confirm limit on an event discovered in-sweep; its own initial research should promote it on the same two Federal Reserve primaries this one cites. Checked 2026-09-06
notes: DISCOVERED during the industrial-production-2026-11-17 initial-research adjacency sweep (2026-09-06). Why it is proposed rather than merely noted: 2026-12-16 already carries two tracked events (mtis-2026-12-16, retail-sales-2026-12-16) and the Atlanta Fed schedules a GDPNow vintage there naming exactly three releases — retail sales, inventories and industrial production — of which the calendar tracked two and missed this one. That is the same gap the mtis-2026-11-17 sweep found on 2026-11-17 and closed by proposing this event's own id; the December date reproduces it one month on. It is also the natural control for the November print: same 09:15 hour, same retail co-release, but November 2026 data is month 2 of the nowcast quarter rather than month 1, and the position class measured this session runs 0.3515pp of GDP-nowcast movement at month 1 against 0.2007pp at month 2 (n=44 and 46 G.17 vintages). Impact LOW and symbols empty on the same measured grounds as the November edition: the report's own Equipment channel moves a median 0.0159pp across 143 G.17 vintages while PCE moves 0.0852pp, no macro-keyed house playbook exists (grep re-run 2026-09-06, 0 hits), and no instrument attaches. Deliberately NOT proposed alongside it: the 2026-09-18 and 2026-10-16 G.17 editions, which are real dated Board-scheduled releases but stand alone at 09:15 with no co-release — and the Atlanta Fed schedules no GDPNow vintage on either, matching this session's finding that a standalone G.17 date is indistinguishable from an ordinary session. Proposed as an estimate; nothing here licenses an entry.
